description:
FILED s419 (Fable), found by the #119 probe sweep.  PRE-EXISTING, not a
#119 regression (the fix changed which string is matched, not the return).

  my $q = "abc";
  my $n = ($q =~ s/zzz/x/);
  print "got: <$n>\n";     # perl: <>   (empty string, numerically 0)
                           # PCL:  <0>  (the number zero)

perl documents s/// as returning the number of substitutions "or false" --
and its false is PL_sv_no, the dualvar ("", 0).  PCL returns integer 0,
which prints as "0".  Same question for tr/// with no matches (perl returns
0 there -- a count -- so tr is probably NOT affected; probe first) and for
m// in scalar context (PCL already returns nil/"" -- verify).

FIX SHAPE: return "" (or the shared false constant the runtime uses for
boolean ops) from do-regex-subst when count is 0 and not /r.  CHECK USES:
arithmetic consumers ("" + 1 == 1, same as 0 + 1) are safe; string
consumers print differently, which is the divergence.  A sweep TOTAL/LOST
run is the bar (some baseline rows may assert the current "0").
DONE s420.  do-regex-subst returns "" instead of 0 when no substitution
happened (and not /r).  Probed 9 shapes against perl: tr/// really does return
a count of 0 there (NOT affected), m// already answered "", and every
arithmetic/boolean consumer is unchanged ("" numifies to 0 and is false).
Sweep: 0 new, 0 fixed.  Guard: Pl/t/match-vars-01.t row 28.
title: s/// (and tr///?) no-match returns 0 where perl returns "" (empty string)
